title: Shock from illness or injury
summary: Call emergency services, use a safe lying position, keep warm, and control an obvious cause such as bleeding.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Position for Shock
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: Call emergency services immediately and describe the likely cause.
Keep an alert person lying on their back. If this worsens breathing, allow the most comfortable breathing position; use the left side in late pregnancy when practical.
Control severe bleeding, loosen tight clothing, and protect from cold with a blanket.
If there is no trauma or pain, raising the feet about 15 to 30 cm (6 to 12 in) may be reasonable. Lower them if pain, discomfort, or worsening occurs.
Monitor alertness and breathing. Use the recovery position if alertness falls but breathing remains normal; start CPR for absent or abnormal breathing.
prohibitions: Do not give food, drink, or oral medicine.
Do not make the person stand or walk.
Do not raise the legs when leg, pelvis, abdomen, chest, or spine injury is possible.

emergencyCall.text: Signs of shock can indicate life-threatening bleeding or illness; call emergency services now.
